A sketch pattern's spacing from a driven dimension of its own sketch (mitcad#2057, GitHub #470), on a reported design (opened with --open, never committed; tools/cli/pattern-spacing-driven-reported-test.cmake): Sketch14 (F1) has a 30 x 200 rectangle fixed at the origin, a construction line c35 from its corner p5 to the middle of its right side measured by the driven length k11 (d5), and a pattern k12 of the rectangle along that line, its spacing d6 written from the driving dimensions. Spacing d5 was refused: the sketch itself could not use it outside its driving dimensions.
The pattern's own spacing parameter given the reference, as the parameter table does: accepted, the copies where they were.
The spacing set to d5 itself, as the Pattern panel does.
The copy of p5 (p41) lies d5 along the pattern's direction from it, at the middle of the right side: entities c1-c4, p5-p9, p34, c35, then the copies p40-p43 of p8, p5, p7, p6.
A wider rectangle: the driven length measures again and the copies move by the new measure in the same recompute (the direction is stored, so they leave the line).
